translation: When yang-qi is exuberant, [the eyes] open wide (chen mu); when yin-qi is exuberant, [the eyes] close (ming mu); in heat reversal take Foot Taiyang and Shaoyang. The Jia Yi jing says: When a person is ill with the eyes closed and unable to see, the wei-qi remains in the yin and cannot move into the yang; remaining in the yin then the yin-qi is exuberant, with the yin-qi exuberant the Yin Qiao is full; being unable to enter the yang then the yang-qi is deficient, and therefore the eyes close. When a person is ill with the eyes unable to close, the wei-qi cannot enter the yin and constantly remains in the yang; remaining in the yang then the yang-qi is full, with the yang-qi full the Yang Qiao is exuberant; being unable to enter the yin then the yin-qi is deficient, and therefore the eyes do not close.
